new_statements.relation_note: Author (team linguist doing the phonemic analysis from a c. 400-item checked wordlist) states in passing that tone and rhythm are not used to distinguish words in Kovol; no stress-placement rule; part 4 gives six vowel phonemes /i e ɛ u o ɑ/ and [l]~[r] as one phoneme; an Ethnos360 orthography was later approved and primers drafted (2025), implying an unpublished phonemic write-up exists.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Negative statement only: neither tone nor 'rhythm' (stress/timing) is lexically contrastive in Kovol; where stress falls is not said.
new_statements.identity_note: 'Kovol people', c. 1,000, 7 villages in the Adelbert mountains, Madang Province; dialect/village names Imengis and Matat match the Ethnologue/Joshua Project dialect names for Kobol/Kovol [kgu] (Imengis, Kobumbua, Koguman, Matat); Ethnologue 28 uses 'Kovol' as primary name for kgu; neighbouring language named as 'Pal' (= abw, the other Omosan language). Not Koguman of any other province. [name in source: Kovol; pages web posts; statement in part 1, section 'Phonetics: 1 symbol for 1 sound'; vowel inventory in part 4; dialects (Imengis, Matat) in 'The Pick Your Alphabet meeting']
